plans.note: Section 9 (Limitation of Liability) is the primary locus; check mutuality, cap amount and whether indemnity (sec-8-2) and confidentiality (sec-10) breaches are carved out. Section 8's disclaimer may interact with the cap.

Section 8 INDEMNIFICATION should carry Commerce One's third-party IP indemnity in our favour as licensee/host; verify our reciprocal indemnity is narrow and that the sec-9 cap does not swallow it. Trademark use (sec-6) may raise a related indemnity hook.

Grant of Rights plus the defined terms CORIO MARKET SEGMENT and TERRITORY suggest field-of-use or competitive restraints on us; also scan Exhibit D (sales and marketing cooperation) and Miscellaneous for any covenant not to license or build competing procurement software.

Check Section 2 Grant of Rights and the CORIO MARKET SEGMENT / TERRITORY definitions for any obligation on us to host or resell only Commerce One software; Exhibit D cooperation terms may add de facto exclusivity.

Pricing (Exhibit B), revenue sharing and payment terms are where any most-favoured-customer language would sit; likely no MFN, and any MFN running in our favour would be acceptable — only flag one obliging us to give Commerce One best terms.
Miscellaneous is the usual home; also check Confidentiality and the support-contacts exhibit for any hiring restriction arising from personnel contact. Probably absent.

Section 11 Term and Termination governs; confirm we have a convenience exit on notice without penalty and that Commerce One cannot terminate mid-term at will, and check sec-4/Exhibit B for any termination charges or accelerated fees.
Renewal mechanics and non-renewal notice window should be in Section 11; renewal pricing uplift, if any, would appear in Exhibit B pricing or payment terms.

Miscellaneous should carry governing law, venue and any arbitration reference (the defined term RULES suggests an arbitral rule set); verify law is NY/DE/CA/E&W and that disputes go to courts rather than foreign arbitration.

Assignment and change-of-control language sits in Miscellaneous; confirm we may assign to affiliates and successors and that Commerce One cannot terminate on our change of control (a real risk given the ASP/competitor dynamic).

Grant of Rights and the DEVELOPMENTS / EMPLOYEE NDA-INVENTION AGREEMENT definitions are the key spots for ownership of modifications and of our customer data; check that nothing assigns our data, configurations or Corio-created developments to Commerce One. Escrow (sec-12) and Confidentiality are related.

Section 2 Grant of Rights read with the SOFTWARE, DEMONSTRATION SOFTWARE, CUSTOMER(S), SOFTWARE USER and TERRITORY definitions and Exhibit A; confirm the licence extends to our affiliates, contractors and hosted end customers and is not revocable at will.

Revenue-sharing fees usually bring a records-and-audit right against us; look in Section 4 Fees, the revenue sharing block and Exhibit B payment terms for notice, frequency, location and cost-shifting terms.
Check Fees and Exhibit B payment terms for late-payment interest or penalty-style charges payable by us, and Section 11 for termination penalties; service credits running to us are acceptable.

Section 7 Warranties and Disclaimer plus the Acceptance Test and Warranty Period definitions set duration and remedy; Section 5 (maintenance) and Exhibit C support/priority definitions supply the ongoing performance commitment.
No insurance heading appears in the outline; if absent, note that Commerce One personnel access and data exposure warrant a standard insurance covenant in Miscellaneous.

Exhibit B pricing, revenue sharing fees and the IMPLEMENTATION FEE / payment terms are where minimum guarantees or take-or-pay volumes would appear; pair with Section 11 to confirm an exit exists if a minimum is imposed.

Section 11 should address post-termination effects (wind-down for hosted end customers, return or destruction of materials and data); Section 12 source code escrow is the related continuity mechanism. Flag if no transition assistance or data-return obligation exists.
